items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขออนุญาตและการอนุญาต

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
B: ______
choices: No, I'm not taking it anywhere.
No, it's free. Please sit down.

explanation.en: "Is this seat taken?" asks whether someone is already using it. "No, it's free" means A can sit there. "Yes, please take it" contradicts itself, because "Yes" means the seat is occupied.
explanation.th: "Is this seat taken?" ถามว่ามีคนนั่งแล้วหรือยัง คำตอบที่ถูกคือ "No, it's free. Please sit down." ส่วน "Yes, please take it" ขัดแย้งในตัว เพราะ "Yes" แปลว่า มีคนนั่งแล้ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขอโทษและการตอบรับคำขอโทษ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I'm afraid I've spilled coffee all over your notes. I'm really sorry.
B: ______
choices: Oh well, accidents happen. I can print them again.

explanation.en: B accepts the apology and reduces A's worry: "Accidents happen. I can print them again." "Not at all. Go ahead" gives permission, and "It's my pleasure" answers thanks.
explanation.th: B ตอบรับคำขอโทษและทำให้ A สบายใจ คือ "Oh well, accidents happen. I can print them again." ส่วน "Not at all. Go ahead." ใช้อนุญาต และ "It's my pleasure" ใช้ตอบคำขอบคุณ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเข้าใจสำนวนในบทสนทนา

topic.th: บทสนทนา: สำนวนและวลีที่ใช้บ่อย

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: Did you hand in the science project on time?
B: Only just! We finished it ______ — five minutes before the deadline.
choices: at the drop of a hat
on the spur of the moment

explanation.en: "In the nick of time" means "just before it was too late", matching "five minutes before the deadline". "Once in a blue moon" means "very rarely", "on the spur of the moment" means "without planning", and "at the drop of a hat" means "immediately, without hesitation".
explanation.th: "in the nick of time" แปลว่า ทันเวลาพอดี ตรงกับ "five minutes before the deadline" ส่วน "once in a blue moon" แปลว่า นาน ๆ ครั้ง "on the spur of the moment" แปลว่า ทำโดยไม่ได้วางแผน และ "at the drop of a hat" แปลว่า ทันทีโดยไม่ลังเล

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Checking understanding and asking for clarification
skill.th: การตรวจสอบความเข้าใจและการขอคำอธิบาย

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: You can't miss the café — it's right opposite the post office.
B: ______
A: Yes, exactly. Just across the road from it.
choices: So it's next to the post office, on the same side?
Sorry, why can't I miss it?
So it's on the other side of the road from the post office?
So I mustn't miss the post office?

explanation.en: "Opposite" means "facing, on the other side", and A confirms "just across the road", so B checked: "So it's on the other side of the road …?" "You can't miss it" means "it's easy to find", not a rule.
explanation.th: "opposite" แปลว่า อยู่ตรงข้าม และ A ยืนยันว่า "just across the road" B จึงถามตรวจสอบว่า "So it's on the other side of the road …?" ส่วน "You can't miss it" แปลว่า หาง่ายมาก ไม่ใช่คำสั่งห้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขอและการให้คำแนะนำ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I can't decide whether to join the debate club or the robotics club.
B: ______
choices: How about to join the robotics club?
Why not try both for a few weeks and then decide?

explanation.en: "Why not + base form" is a natural way to suggest something. "How about" needs "-ing" ("How about joining"), "should" is followed by the base form without "to", and "It's up to me" should be "It's up to you".
explanation.th: "Why not + กริยาช่องหนึ่ง" ใช้เสนอแนะได้อย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ ส่วน "How about" ต้องตามด้วย V-ing "should" ตามด้วยกริยาช่องหนึ่งโดยไม่มี to และ "It's up to me" ควรเป็น "It's up to you"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับและปฏิเสธคำเชิญอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: A few of us are going for dinner after the match. Fancy joining us?
B: ______
A: Great! We'll meet at the main gate at seven.
choices: I'm afraid I'll have to give it a miss.
I don't fancy it, to be honest.

explanation.en: A replies "Great!" and arranges a meeting time, so B accepted: "Count me in!" means "include me". The other three replies all refuse the invitation.
explanation.th: A ตอบว่า "Great!" และนัดเวลา แสดงว่า B ตอบรับ "Count me in!" แปลว่า นับฉันด้วย ส่วนอีกสามคำตอบเป็นการปฏิเสธคำชวน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความเห็นด้วยและไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I reckon online lessons will completely replace schools one day.
B: ______ Students need to meet each other face to face.
choices: That's just what I was thinking.
I can't say I agree with you there.
I couldn't have put it better myself.

explanation.en: B's reason argues against A, so B disagrees: "I can't say I agree with you there." "You can say that again" is an idiom meaning "I strongly agree", as are the other two replies.
explanation.th: เหตุผลของ B แย้งความคิดของ A จึงต้องเป็นการไม่เห็นด้วย คือ "I can't say I agree with you there." ส่วน "You can say that again" เป็นสำนวนแปลว่า เห็นด้วยอย่างยิ่ง เช่นเดียวกับอีกสองคำตอบ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การร้องเรียนและการรับมือกับคำร้องเรียน

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: The repairman said he'd come at nine, and it's already half past eleven!
B: ______
choices: Better late than never — he's early!
Never mind. He's probably finished by now.
Lucky you. He's always so punctual.
That's so annoying. Have you tried ringing the company?

explanation.en: A is complaining that the repairman is very late, so B shows understanding and suggests action. The other replies wrongly treat him as early, punctual or already finished.
explanation.th: A บ่นว่าช่างมาสายมาก B จึงควรแสดงความเข้าใจและแนะนำให้โทรหาบริษัท ส่วนคำตอบอื่นเข้าใจผิดว่าช่างมาเร็ว ตรงเวลา หรือทำงานเสร็จแล้ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้คำที่ใช้คู่กันอย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The new law will ______ effect on 1 January, so shops must be ready by then."

explanation.en: A law "takes effect", meaning it starts to apply. "Make", "do" and "bring" do not form this expression.
explanation.th: กฎหมาย "takes effect" แปลว่า เริ่มมีผลบังคับใช้ ส่วน "make", "do" และ "bring" ไม่ใช้ในสำนวนนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Finding a word with a similar meaning
skill.th: การหาคำที่มีความหมายใกล้เคียง

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the phrase closest in meaning to "meticulous" in this sentence.
"She is meticulous about her work; she checks every detail twice."

explanation.en: Checking every detail twice shows she is "meticulous": extremely careful and precise. "Rather careless" is the opposite.
explanation.th: การตรวจทุกรายละเอียดสองรอบแสดงว่าเธอ "meticulous" คือ พิถีพิถัน ละเอียดรอบคอบมาก ส่วน "rather careless" มีความหมายตรงข้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Forming words with prefixes and suffixes
skill.th: การสร้างคำด้วยอุปสรรคและปัจจัย

topic.th: คำศัพท์: การสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Plastic waste is a major ______ to marine life."

explanation.en: After "a major", a noun is needed: "a major threat to". "Threaten" is a verb, and "threatening" and "threatened" are adjectives or verb forms.
explanation.th: หลัง "a major" ต้องใช้คำนาม คือ "threat" (ภัยคุกคาม) ส่วน "threaten" เป็นกริยา และ "threatening", "threatened" เป็นคุณศัพท์หรือรูปกริยา

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Forming words with prefixes and suffixes
skill.th: การสร้างคำด้วยอุปสรรคและปัจจัย

topic.th: คำศัพท์: การสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The witness's story was so ______ that the police doubted every word of it."

explanation.en: The negative form of "plausible" (believable) is "implausible". Before the letter p, the prefix in- becomes im-, as in "impossible" and "impatient".
explanation.th: รูปปฏิเสธของ "plausible" (น่าเชื่อ) คือ "implausible" เพราะอุปสรรค in- จะเปลี่ยนเป็น im- เมื่ออยู่หน้าตัว p เช่น impossible, impatient

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้กริยาวลี (phrasal verbs)

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"When sales fell sharply, the company had to ______ fifty workers."

explanation.en: To "lay off" workers means to stop employing them because there is not enough work. "Lay down" means "put down", "set off" means "start a journey", and "turn down" means "refuse".
explanation.th: "lay off" แปลว่า เลิกจ้างเพราะงานไม่พอ ส่วน "lay down" แปลว่า วางลง "set off" แปลว่า ออกเดินทาง และ "turn down" แปลว่า ปฏิเสธ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้คำที่ใช้คู่กันอย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"After months of argument, the two sides finally ______ an agreement."

explanation.en: We "reach an agreement". "Arrive" needs "at", "make up" means "invent" or "become friends again", and we "win" a game, not an agreement.
explanation.th: คำที่ใช้คู่กันคือ "reach an agreement" (บรรลุข้อตกลง) ส่วน "arrive" ต้องมี "at" "make up" แปลว่า แต่งเรื่องหรือคืนดีกัน และ "win" ใช้กับการแข่งขัน

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Finding a word with the opposite meaning
skill.th: การหาคำที่มีความหมายตรงข้าม

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "scarce".
"Fresh water is scarce in the desert, so every drop is precious."

explanation.en: "Scarce" means "in short supply"; the opposite is "plentiful". "Rare" is close in meaning, not opposite.
explanation.th: "scarce" แปลว่า ขาดแคลน หายาก คำตรงข้ามคือ "plentiful" (มีมากมาย) ส่วน "rare" มีความหมายใกล้เคียง ไม่ใช่ตรงข้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Choosing the word that fits the context
skill.th: การเลือกคำให้เหมาะกับบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Her explanation was so ______ that even the youngest students understood it immediately."

explanation.en: If even the youngest students understood at once, the explanation was simple and clear: "straightforward". "Complicated" and "ambiguous" would make it hard to understand.
explanation.th: ถ้าแม้แต่นักเรียนที่เด็กที่สุดก็เข้าใจทันที คำอธิบายต้อง "straightforward" (ตรงไปตรงมา เข้าใจง่าย) ส่วน "complicated" และ "ambiguous" จะทำให้เข้าใจยาก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้กริยาวลี (phrasal verbs)

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"We've ______ sugar. Could you buy some on your way home?"

explanation.en: To "run out of" something means to have none left. "Run into" means "meet by chance", "run over" means "hit with a vehicle", and "run away from" means "escape".
explanation.th: "run out of" แปลว่า หมด ไม่เหลือ ส่วน "run into" แปลว่า บังเอิญเจอ "run over" แปลว่า ขับรถชน และ "run away from" แปลว่า หนีจาก

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Choosing the word that fits the context
skill.th: การเลือกคำให้เหมาะกับบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Can I ______ your pen for a moment? I'll give it back straight away."

explanation.en: The speaker wants to take and use the pen for a short time, so "borrow" is correct. You "lend" something to another person; "rent" involves paying, and "owe" means "need to pay back".
explanation.th: ผู้พูดขอเอาปากกาไปใช้ชั่วคราว จึงใช้ "borrow" (ขอยืม) ส่วน "lend" แปลว่า ให้ยืม "rent" คือ เช่าโดยจ่ายเงิน และ "owe" แปลว่า ติดหนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยค passive

topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: กาลและประโยค passive

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The thief ______ by the police yesterday afternoon."

explanation.en: The police caught the thief, so the passive is needed, and "yesterday afternoon" requires the past simple: "was caught". "Has been caught" cannot be used with a finished past time.
explanation.th: ตำรวจเป็นผู้จับ ขโมยจึงเป็นผู้ถูกกระทำ ต้องใช้ passive และ "yesterday afternoon" ต้องใช้ past simple คือ "was caught" ส่วน "has been caught" ใช้กับเวลาในอดีตที่จบแล้วไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้ gerund หรือ infinitive หลังกริยา

topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: gerund, infinitive และ modal verbs

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I don't want to risk ______ the last train, so let's leave now."

explanation.en: "Risk" is followed by a gerund: "risk missing".
explanation.th: กริยา "risk" ตามด้วย gerund (V-ing) คือ "risk missing"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับประธานกับกริยาหลังคำวิเศษณ์เชิงปฏิเสธ

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Under no circumstances ______ open the emergency door while the train is moving."

explanation.en: A sentence beginning with the negative phrase "Under no circumstances" needs inversion: "should passengers open".
explanation.th: ประโยคที่ขึ้นต้นด้วยวลีปฏิเสธ "Under no circumstances" ต้องสลับกริยาช่วยไว้หน้าประธาน คือ "should passengers open"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไข (if-clauses)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"______ you need any help with the project, please don't hesitate to call me."

explanation.en: "Should you need …" is an inverted, formal form of "If you need …". "Were you need" and "Had you need" are ungrammatical, and "Unless" gives the opposite meaning.
explanation.th: "Should you need …" เป็นรูปสลับที่เป็นทางการของ "If you need …" ส่วน "Were you need" และ "Had you need" ผิดไวยากรณ์ และ "Unless" ให้ความหมายตรงข้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความปรารถนาและความเสียดาย (wish / if only)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"It's getting dark. It's time we ______ home."

explanation.en: "It's time + subject" is followed by the past simple with a present meaning: "It's time we went home."
explanation.th: "It's time + ประธาน" ตามด้วย past simple แต่มีความหมายปัจจุบัน คือ "It's time we went home."

items.subject: eng

skill.th: อนุประโยคขยายนาม (relative clauses)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"That's the hospital ______ I was born."

explanation.en: The clause "I was born" is complete and refers to a place, so the relative adverb "where" is needed. "Which" or "that" would need "in" at the end ("which I was born in").
explanation.th: ประโยค "I was born" สมบูรณ์แล้วและพูดถึงสถานที่ จึงใช้ "where" ส่วน "which" หรือ "that" ต้องมี "in" ท้ายประโยค

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเล่าคำพูด (reported speech)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I'll call you tomorrow," he said.
"He said he ______ me the following day."

explanation.en: In reported speech after "said", "will" usually changes to "would", and "tomorrow" becomes "the following day": "he would call me".
explanation.th: ในการเล่าคำพูดหลัง "said" คำว่า "will" มักเปลี่ยนเป็น "would" และ "tomorrow" เปลี่ยนเป็น "the following day" จึงได้ "he would call me"

items.stem:

items.passage:
For most of human history, anyone who looked up on a clear night could see thousands of stars and the pale band of the Milky Way. Today, (1) ______, more than a third of the world's population can no longer see it from where they live. The cause is light pollution: the glow (2) ______ by street lamps, advertising signs and buildings that stay lit all night.

Light pollution is not only a problem for astronomers. Many animals depend (3) ______ darkness. Baby sea turtles, for example, find the ocean by moving towards the brightest horizon, which used to be the moonlit sea. Near brightly lit beaches, they often crawl the wrong way and die before (4) ______ the water. Migrating birds can also become confused, circling lit towers until they are exhausted.

Humans are affected too. Bright light at night can (5) ______ with the production of melatonin, the hormone that controls sleep. Some researchers believe this may (6) ______ to health problems over time.

The good news is that, unlike many other kinds of pollution, light pollution can be reversed almost instantly. Simply switching off unnecessary lights, or using lamps that point downwards instead of into the sky, makes a (7) ______ difference. Several towns around the world have already been recognised as "dark sky communities" after changing their street lighting. Had more cities followed their example, millions more children (8) ______ the Milky Way with their own eyes by now.
items.stem: Which choice best fits blank (1)?

explanation.en: The sentence contrasts the past (everyone could see the stars) with today (many cannot), so "however" fits.
explanation.th: ประโยคนี้แสดงความขัดแย้งระหว่างอดีต (ทุกคนเห็นดาว) กับปัจจุบัน (หลายคนมองไม่เห็น) จึงใช้ "however"

items.passage:
The Last Ferry

By the time Anan reached the pier, the last ferry to the island was already pulling away. He waved and shouted, but the engine was too loud, and the boat grew smaller until it was only a white dot on the dark water.

He sat down heavily on his backpack. His phone battery had died an hour earlier, and the only other person in sight was an old woman packing up a stall that sold grilled squid. Anan had promised his mother he would be home before nine. Now it was almost eight, and the next ferry would not leave until six the following morning.

"Missed it?" the woman called. Anan nodded, too embarrassed to speak. She studied him for a moment, then pointed at a small fishing boat tied to the end of the pier. "My son goes back to the island at half past eight," she said. "He won't mind one more passenger — if you help him carry the ice."

The ice turned out to be twelve heavy boxes. By the time the last one was on board, Anan's arms were shaking and his shirt was soaked. The woman's son, a quiet man called Wit, simply handed him a bottle of cold water and started the engine.

The crossing took forty minutes. Wit said almost nothing, but halfway across he switched off the lights and told Anan to look over the side. The water was full of tiny blue sparks, flashing wherever the boat disturbed it. "Plankton," Wit said. "They glow when something moves them." Anan had lived near the sea all his life and had never seen anything like it.

When they reached the island, his mother was waiting on the jetty, her face tight with worry. She had been about to call the police. Anan expected to be told off, and he was — but only after she had hugged him for a very long time.

Years later, Anan would tell the story often. Strangely, he never described it as the night he missed the ferry. He always called it the night the sea lit up.

Why Cities Are Getting Hotter

On a hot afternoon in April, the temperature in central Bangkok can be several degrees higher than in the rice fields an hour's drive away. This difference is known as the "urban heat island" effect, and it is becoming one of the most serious challenges facing cities around the world.

The main cause is the material cities are built from. Concrete, asphalt and brick absorb the sun's energy during the day and release it slowly at night, so city streets often stay warm long after sunset. Dark surfaces, such as roads and roofs, are particularly effective at trapping heat. At the same time, cities have far fewer trees and open fields than the countryside. Plants cool the air naturally by releasing water through their leaves, a process called transpiration. When green spaces are replaced by buildings, this natural air conditioning disappears.

Human activity adds to the problem. Cars, factories and, ironically, air conditioners all release heat into the streets. The more people use air conditioning to escape the heat, the hotter the air outside becomes, which in turn encourages even more people to switch theirs on.

The consequences are not only uncomfortable. Extreme heat puts pressure on electricity supplies and can be dangerous for elderly people, young children and outdoor workers. Some studies also suggest that hot cities suffer from worse air quality, as heat speeds up the chemical reactions that form smog.

Fortunately, there are solutions. Painting roofs white or light grey can reflect much of the sunlight that would otherwise be absorbed. Singapore has encouraged "green roofs" and walls covered in plants, while Medellín in Colombia created a network of tree-lined "green corridors" that has reportedly lowered temperatures along them by around two degrees. Even small changes, such as planting shade trees in school playgrounds, can make a noticeable difference.

None of these measures can stop global temperatures from rising. However, they can make cities more pleasant and safer places to live — and as more of the world's population moves into urban areas, that matters more than ever.

choices: How planting trees can stop global warming
Why Bangkok is the hottest city in the world

The history of air conditioning in Asia

explanation.en: The text explains the causes of the urban heat island effect and then describes solutions. It says these measures "cannot stop global temperatures from rising", so the tree option is wrong.

Progress Should Not Mean Knocking Down Our Past

Last month, the row of wooden shophouses at the end of my street was demolished. For nearly a century, those buildings had housed a noodle shop, a tailor, a goldsmith and a family who repaired bicycles. In their place, a developer plans to build a twenty-storey condominium with a car park and a convenience store — the same convenience store that already exists on almost every corner of the city.

I understand the arguments for redevelopment. Cities need housing, and old buildings can be expensive to maintain and difficult to make safe. Nobody wants to live in a place that is falling apart. But we should be honest about what is lost when a neighbourhood's history is replaced by glass and concrete. Old buildings are not just structures; they are a record of how ordinary people lived and worked. Once they are gone, no amount of money can bring them back.

There is also an economic case for protecting them. Visitors rarely travel across the world to photograph a shopping mall that looks exactly like the one at home. They come for character: narrow lanes, family businesses and architecture that could only exist in that place. Cities such as George Town in Malaysia and Hoi An in Vietnam have shown that carefully restored historic districts can attract millions of tourists and support thousands of small businesses.

None of this means that cities must be frozen in time. The best approach is to combine old and new: to restore historic buildings for modern uses, such as cafés, studios and small hotels, while building new housing on land that is genuinely empty. What we need is planning that asks not only how much a building is worth, but what it means to the people who live around it.

If we fail to ask that question, our children will grow up in cities that are newer and taller — but poorer in every way that cannot be measured.

items.passage:
Progress Should Not Mean Knocking Down Our Past

Last month, the row of wooden shophouses at the end of my street was demolished. For nearly a century, those buildings had housed a noodle shop, a tailor, a goldsmith and a family who repaired bicycles. In their place, a developer plans to build a twenty-storey condominium with a car park and a convenience store — the same convenience store that already exists on almost every corner of the city.

I understand the arguments for redevelopment. Cities need housing, and old buildings can be expensive to maintain and difficult to make safe. Nobody wants to live in a place that is falling apart. But we should be honest about what is lost when a neighbourhood's history is replaced by glass and concrete. Old buildings are not just structures; they are a record of how ordinary people lived and worked. Once they are gone, no amount of money can bring them back.

There is also an economic case for protecting them. Visitors rarely travel across the world to photograph a shopping mall that looks exactly like the one at home. They come for character: narrow lanes, family businesses and architecture that could only exist in that place. Cities such as George Town in Malaysia and Hoi An in Vietnam have shown that carefully restored historic districts can attract millions of tourists and support thousands of small businesses.

None of this means that cities must be frozen in time. The best approach is to combine old and new: to restore historic buildings for modern uses, such as cafés, studios and small hotels, while building new housing on land that is genuinely empty. What we need is planning that asks not only how much a building is worth, but what it means to the people who live around it.

If we fail to ask that question, our children will grow up in cities that are newer and taller — but poorer in every way that cannot be measured.
items.stem: How does the writer feel about the convenience store planned for the new building?
choices: Worried that its prices will be too high
Unimpressed, because the city already has the same store almost everywhere
Neutral, because it is only a small detail
Pleased, because it will be useful for local residents

explanation.en: The writer stresses that it is "the same convenience store that already exists on almost every corner", contrasting it with the unique shops that were lost. This shows disappointment, not pleasure or neutrality.
